title: Finite-mode Fock, Gaussian and Bogoliubov foundations

items.title: Finite-mode Fock to Schrödinger identification
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $r\ge1$, let $H=\mathbb C^r$ with orthonormal basis
$e_1,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{\otimes_s n}$
be the bosonic Fock space with vacuum $\Omega$ and creation and annihilation
operators $a_j^*,a_j$ from
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For
$N=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb N_0^r$, set
$$|N\rangle:=\prod_{j=1}^r\frac{(a_j^*)^{n_j}}{\sqrt{n_j!}}\Omega.$$
Let $g_N(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r g_{n_j}(x_j)$ be the normalized product Hermite
function from [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]].
Then $(|N\rangle)_N$ and $(g_N)_N$ are complete orthonormal families, and the
map $\mathcal U|N\rangle=g_N$ extends uniquely to a unitary
$$\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^r)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^r).$$
On the algebraic finite-particle span, $\mathcal U a_j\mathcal U^{-1}$ and
$\mathcal U a_j^*\mathcal U^{-1}$ are respectively
$(x_j+\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ and $(x_j-\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ on product
Hermite functions. In particular the quadratures
$$Q_j=\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j+a_j^*),\qquad P_j=-i\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j-a_j^*)$$
act there as multiplication by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ and as
$-i\sqrt\hbar\,\partial_{x_j}$, respectively. These are core identities;
they do not assert that a finite number cutoff preserves the canonical
commutation relations.

references.title: Phan Thành Nam, Mathematical Quantum Mechanics II, Chapter 5 §§5.1–5.2, pp. 114–124
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, §8.3, pp. 177–179

items.title: Finite symplectic generator factorization
items.statement:
Let $r\ge1$, $J_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_r\\-I_r&0\end{pmatrix}$, and
$$\operatorname{Sp}(2r,\mathbb R)=\{S\in M_{2r}(\mathbb R):S^TJ_0S=J_0\}.$$
Every $S\in\operatorname{Sp}(2r,\mathbb R)$ is a finite product of matrices
of the following three types and their inverses:
$$U_X=\begin{pmatrix}I&X\\0&I\end{pmatrix},\quad L_Y=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\Y&I\end{pmatrix},\quad D_A=\begin{pmatrix}A&0\\0&A^{-T}\end{pmatrix},$$
where $X,Y$ are real symmetric and $A$ is real invertible. Partial Fourier
rotations, which act by $(q_j,p_j)\mapsto(-p_j,q_j)$ on any selected set of
coordinates and fix the others, are also products of these matrices.
In addition, for every $S$ there is a product $G$ of these generators such
that the upper-left block of $SG$ is invertible.

references.title: Arvind, B. Dutta, N. Mukunda and R. Simon, The Real Symplectic Groups in Quantum Mechanics and Optics, §§II and IV

items.title: Finite-mode quadratures and symplectic data
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, an integer $r\ge1$, and an action scale
$\hbar>0$. Inner products are linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Use the Fock-to-Schrödinger unitary
$\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^r)\to L^2(\mathbb R^r)$ of
[[lem-nrqmx-finite-mode-fock-schr-identification]]. In Schrödinger coordinates
define the self-adjoint quadratures
$$Q_j=\mathcal U^{-1}(\sqrt\hbar\,x_j)\mathcal U,\qquad P_j=\mathcal U^{-1}(-i\sqrt\hbar\,\partial_{x_j})\mathcal U,$$
where $x_j$ is the real multiplication operator on its maximal domain and
$-i\partial_{x_j}$ is defined by conjugating that multiplication operator by
the unitary Fourier transform. Their common Schwartz core satisfies
$$[Q_j,Q_k]=[P_j,P_k]=0,\qquad [Q_j,P_k]=i\hbar\delta_{jk}I.$$
Write $R=(Q_1,P_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_r)^T$ and
$J=\bigoplus_{j=1}^r\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$.
The Weyl unitary labelled by $z=(q_1,p_1,\ldots,q_r,p_r)$ is the unitary
whose grouped-coordinate formula, with $q=(q_1,\ldots,q_r)$ and
$p=(p_1,\ldots,p_r)$, is
$$[W(z)f](x)=e^{i\sqrt\hbar\,q\cdot(x+\sqrt\hbar p/2)}f(x+\sqrt\hbar p).$$
It obeys $W(z)W(z')=e^{-i\hbar z^TJz'/2}W(z+z')$ and is regular and
irreducible. By the finite-dimensional Stone–von Neumann theorem, every
nonzero irreducible regular Weyl system with this finite phase space and this
same nonzero central parameter is unitarily equivalent to it.

A density operator is a positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with
$\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$. Its quadrature second moments are finite when, for
one (equivalently every) spectral expansion
$\rho=\sum_n w_n|\psi_n\rangle\langle\psi_n|$ with $w_n>0$,
$\sum_nw_n\|R_j\psi_n\|^2<\infty$ for every $j$. For such a state define
$$d_j=\sum_nw_n\langle R_j\psi_n,\psi_n\rangle,\qquad V_{jk}=\operatorname{Re}\sum_nw_n \langle(R_j-d_jI)\psi_n,(R_k-d_kI)\psi_n\rangle.$$
These quantities are independent of the chosen orthonormal eigenbasis in
each eigenspace. The state is Gaussian when its Weyl characteristic function
has the form
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho W(z))= \exp\!\left(i z^Td-\tfrac12z^TVz\right)\quad(z\in\mathbb R^{2r}),$$
with real $d$ and real symmetric $V$. Here $R_j$ has units
$\sqrt{\mathrm{action}}$, each Weyl label has units
$1/\sqrt{\mathrm{action}}$, and $V$ has units of action. No finite particle
number truncation is used.

references.title: Christian Weedbrook et al., Gaussian Quantum Information, §§II.A–II.C.1, pp. 4–9
Phan Thành Nam, Mathematical Quantum Mechanics II, §§5.1–5.4, pp. 114–131

items.title: Individual finite symplectic implementers
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. On $L^2(\mathbb R^r)$, for $r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$,
define the Weyl unitaries in grouped label order $(q,p)\in\mathbb R^r\oplus
\mathbb R^r$ by
$$[W(q,p)f](x)=e^{i\sqrt\hbar\,q\cdot(x+\sqrt\hbar p/2)}f(x+\sqrt\hbar p).$$
For $J_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix}$, every
$T\in\operatorname{Sp}(2r,\mathbb R)$ has a unitary $M_T$ such that
$$M_T^*W(z)M_T=W(Tz)\quad(z\in\mathbb R^{2r}).$$
Any two such unitaries differ by a scalar of modulus one. The covariance
identity holds on all of $L^2$; the corresponding unbounded quadrature
identities hold on the common transported Schwartz domain. This is an
individual existence and phase-uniqueness result; it does not identify the
global topology or kernel of a continuously chosen implementer family.

references.title: Arvind, B. Dutta, N. Mukunda and R. Simon, The Real Symplectic Groups in Quantum Mechanics and Optics, §§IV–VI
Phan Thành Nam, Mathematical Quantum Mechanics II, §6.3, pp. 146–156

items.title: Maslov phase parity in a finite generating chart
items.statement:
Use the finite-mode conventions, including their Axiom of Choice assumption, of the finite-mode symplectic-data definition. Let $r\ge1$, $\hbar>0$, and let $S$ be a real finite-mode symplectic matrix
in grouped order $(q,p)$ whose upper-right block $B$ is invertible. Consider
two unitary propagators $U_1,U_2$ obtained from time-dependent real
homogeneous quadratic Hamiltonians (no linear or constant term), both with
classical endpoint $S$. Use the normalization that each propagator starts at
the identity and solves the Schrödinger equation with Planck scale $\hbar$.
Precisely, on a compact interval $[0,T]$ with $T>0$, the real symmetric coefficient matrix $K$ is Lebesgue integrable entrywise, the classical path is the absolutely continuous solution of $\dot S(t)=J_0K(t)S(t)$ with $S(0)=I$, and
$$H_t=\frac14\sum_{a,b=1}^{2r}K_{ab}(t)(R_aR_b+R_bR_a),\qquad J_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_r\\-I_r&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^r)$ has seminorms $p_{\alpha,\beta}(f)=\sup_x|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$ for multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$. A unitary Schwartz automorphism is a unitary on $L^2$ restricting to a continuous linear bijection of $\mathcal S$ with continuous inverse. A normalized propagator is a path of these automorphisms with $U(0)=I$ such that, for each Schwartz vector, its trajectory is absolutely continuous in every Schwartz seminorm and obeys $i\hbar\,\partial_tU(t)f=H_tU(t)f$ almost everywhere. Absolute continuity for a curve means the usual finite disjoint-interval condition for its increments in each seminorm. These conventions include piecewise-smooth Hamiltonian paths.
Then
$$U_2=U_1\quad\text{or}\quad U_2=-U_1.$$
The same conclusion holds after multiplying both propagators by a fixed
normalized quadratic propagator, provided the resulting endpoint lies in a
chart with invertible upper-right block.

references.title: Joel Robbin and Dietmar Salamon, Feynman path integrals on phase space and the metaplectic representation, §§5, 6.4, 8.5
Joel Robbin and Dietmar Salamon, The Maslov index for paths, Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.12

items.title: Finite symplectic implementation by quadratic generators
items.statement:
Assume AC, $r\ge1$, and $\hbar>0$. Let $R=(Q_1,P_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_r)^T$,
$J=\bigoplus_{j=1}^r\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$,
and let $W(z)$ be the regular irreducible Weyl system of
[[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. For every real
$S\in\operatorname{Sp}(2r,\mathbb R)$, there is a unitary $M_S$ on
$L^2(\mathbb R^r)$ such that
$$M_S^*W(z)M_S=W(S^Tz)\qquad(z\in\mathbb R^{2r});$$
equivalently, $M_S^*RM_S=SR$ on the common transported Schwartz core.
Any two such implementers differ by a scalar of modulus one. The same
construction applies in every nonzero irreducible regular representation
with this finite phase space and fixed central parameter $\hbar$, after the
unitary equivalence of
[[thm-nrqmx-finite-weyl-uniqueness-interface]].

There is also a connected topological group
$\operatorname{Mp}(2r,\mathbb R)$ of normalized propagators of real
homogeneous quadratic Hamiltonians on this finite-mode Schrödinger space.
Here a unitary Schwartz automorphism means a unitary on $L^2(\mathbb R^r)$
whose restriction is a continuous linear bijection of the Schwartz space
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^r)$ with continuous inverse. A normalized propagator
starts at the identity and solves $i\hbar\,\partial_tU(t)=H_tU(t)$ for a
real symmetrically ordered quadratic $H_t$ with no linear or scalar term.
Give $\operatorname{Mp}$ the topology of pointwise convergence of $U$ and
$U^{-1}$ on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^r)$ in its Schwartz topology; give
$\operatorname{Sp}(2r,\mathbb R)$ its usual matrix topology.
The map
$$\pi:\operatorname{Mp}(2r,\mathbb R)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sp}(2r,\mathbb R),\qquad M\longmapsto S \quad\text{when }M^*W(z)M=W(S^Tz),$$
is a two-fold covering homomorphism. Its two points over $S$ act by $M_S$
and $-M_S$ when $M_S$ denotes either normalized lift; an arbitrary Weyl
implementer may differ from them by any scalar phase. This connected double
cover and its unitary action are the metaplectic group and metaplectic
representation. All mode counts here are finite; no infinite-mode
implementation claim is part of the statement.

references.title: Joel Robbin and Dietmar Salamon, Feynman path integrals on phase space and the metaplectic representation, §§5–10
Joel Robbin and Dietmar Salamon, The Maslov index for paths, Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.12
Arvind, B. Dutta, N. Mukunda and R. Simon, The Real Symplectic Groups in Quantum Mechanics and Optics, §§IV–VI

items.title: Finite Bogoliubov implementability
items.statement:
Assume AC, $r\ge1$, and the finite-mode Fock conventions of
[[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. Let $U,V\in M_r(\mathbb C)$ obey
$$UU^*-VV^*=I_r,\qquad UV^T=VU^T,$$
where $^*$ is conjugate transpose and $^T$ is transpose without conjugation.
On the finite Hermite core define
$$a'_j=\sum_k(U_{jk}a_k+V_{jk}a_k^*).$$
Then the $a'_j$ satisfy $[a'_j,(a'_k)^*]=\delta_{jk}I$ and
$[a'_j,a'_k]=0$ on that core. The real matrix
$$S_g=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}(U+V)&-\operatorname{Im}(U-V)\\ \operatorname{Im}(U+V)&\operatorname{Re}(U-V)\end{pmatrix}$$
is symplectic in grouped coordinate order $(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_1,\ldots,P_r)$.
There is a unitary $M$ on finite-mode Fock, obtained by transporting an
individual finite symplectic implementer through the Fock–Schrödinger
unitary, such that $M^*aM=a'$ on the transported Schwartz core and
$M^*W(z)M=W(S_g^Tz)$ in grouped Weyl-label order. The transformed vacuum
$M\Omega$ has finite mean number
$$\sum_j\|a_jM\Omega\|^2=\operatorname{tr}(VV^*).$$
No infinite-mode implementability assertion is made.

references.title: Phan Thành Nam, Mathematical Quantum Mechanics II, §6.3, pp. 146–156
Christian Weedbrook et al., Gaussian Quantum Information, §II.A, Eqs. (21)–(25)

items.title: Positive definite Williamson normal form
items.statement:
Let $r\ge1$, $\hbar>0$, and
$J=\bigoplus_{j=1}^r\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$.
For every real symmetric positive definite $2r\times2r$ matrix $V$, there
are an interleaved symplectic matrix $S$ ($S^TJS=J$) and positive numbers
$\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_r$ such that
$$V=S D S^T,\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(\nu_1,\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_r,\nu_r).$$
Moreover,
$$V+i\hbar J/2\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nu_j\ge\hbar/2\ \text{for every }j.$$
Here $A\succeq0$ means the Hermitian matrix $A$ has nonnegative quadratic
form on every complex vector.

references.title: Arvind, B. Dutta, N. Mukunda and R. Simon, The Real Symplectic Groups in Quantum Mechanics and Optics, §IX
Phan Thành Nam, Mathematical Quantum Mechanics II, §6.4, pp. 158–162

items.title: Schwartz density in the joint quadrature graph norm
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, let $r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, and use the
Schrödinger quadratures of [[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. Put
$$D=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^r):x_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^r),\ \partial_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^r)\text{ for every }j\}.$$
For
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{quad}}:=\|f\|_2+\sum_{j=1}^r(\|x_jf\|_2+\|\partial_jf\|_2),$$
the Schwartz space $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^r)$ is dense in $D$. The weak
derivatives in this definition are taken in the distributional sense and
agree with the Fourier-defined momentum
domains in the cited quadrature definition.

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Sobolev Spaces, §1.8, Theorem 1.21 and Remark 1.22
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.8, Theorem 1.21 and Remark 1.22(1),(3),(4), printed pp. 19–21.

references.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Linear Analysis and Partial Differential Equations, §3.4
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.4, Proposition 3.7 and Theorem 3.8, printed pp. 57–58.

items.title: Gaussian covariance and uncertainty
items.statement:
Assume AC, $r\ge1$, $\hbar>0$, and the quadrature, density-operator,
characteristic-function, and covariance definitions of
[[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. For every density operator with
finite quadrature second moments,
$$V+i\hbar J/2\succeq0.$$
If $S$ is symplectic and $M_S$ is any individual implementer with
$M_S^*RM_S=SR$ on the quadrature domains, then for
$\rho_S=M_S\rho M_S^*$ its mean and covariance are
$$d_S=Sd,\qquad V_S=SVS^T,$$
and $\chi_{\rho_S}(z)=\chi_\rho(S^Tz)$. Conversely, for every real vector
$d\in\mathbb R^{2r}$ and real symmetric matrix $V$, the function
$$\chi(z)=\exp\!\left(i z^Td-\tfrac12z^TVz\right)$$
is the Weyl characteristic function of a finite-mode density operator if
and only if $V+i\hbar J/2\succeq0$. This is a conditional mathematical
existence result for the stated finite-mode model; it is not an experimental
claim.

references.title: Christian Weedbrook et al., Gaussian Quantum Information, §§II.A and II.C.1, pp. 4–9
Phan Thành Nam, Mathematical Quantum Mechanics II, §§5.4 and 6.5, pp. 128–131, 166–169

title: Finite-mode Fock, Gaussian and Bogoliubov foundations — Examples

items.title: Single-mode squeeze statistics
items.statement:
For one mode with $\hbar>0$, let $\Omega$ be the vacuum and define the
unitary dilation on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ by
$$[U_sf](x)=e^{-s/2}f(e^{-s}x),\qquad s\in\mathbb R.$$
Then
$$U_s^*aU_s=\cosh(s)a+\sinh(s)a^*$$
on the transported Schwartz core. The squeezed vacuum $U_s\Omega$ has mean
number $\sinh^2(s)$ and quadrature means zero and variances
$$\operatorname{Var}(Q)=\frac{\hbar}{2}e^{2s},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(P)=\frac{\hbar}{2}e^{-2s}.$$
Its covariance determinant is $\hbar^2/4$. The implementer orientation is
the pullback convention displayed here; replacing $s$ by $-s$ interchanges
the two variances.

references.title: Christian Weedbrook et al., Gaussian Quantum Information, §II.B.3, Eqs. (32)–(33)
Phan Thành Nam, Mathematical Quantum Mechanics II, §6.3, pp. 146–151

items.title: Finite-mode implementability does not supply an infinite-mode limit
items.statement:
Fix $s\ne0$. For each finite $N\ge1$, apply independently to $N$ vacuum modes
the one-mode dilation $[U_sf](x)=e^{-s/2}f(e^{-s}x)$. The
resulting finite-mode unitary exists, its mean total number is
$$N\sinh^2(s),$$
and the magnitude of its overlap with the $N$-mode vacuum is
$$|\langle\Omega_N,U_s^{\otimes N}\Omega_N\rangle| =(\cosh s)^{-N/2}\longrightarrow0.$$
These exact finite-$N$ calculations exhibit quantities that are not uniform
in mode number. They do not prove an infinite-mode non-implementability
theorem and do not assign a limiting density operator or measurement.

references.title: Phan Thành Nam, Mathematical Quantum Mechanics II, §6.3, pp. 146–156
Arvind, B. Dutta, N. Mukunda and R. Simon, The Real Symplectic Groups in Quantum Mechanics and Optics, §VI
